judged_text: The reference mapping now takes externalCalendarId from result.externalId, which CalendarManager only populates from the caller-supplied destination on the credentialId path (the credential-less fan-out calls createEvent with no externalId), and drops the review-base value result.credentialId for non-calendar (video) references. Bookings created through the credential-less fan-out get BookingReference rows with a null externalCalendarId where review-base persisted destinationCalendar.externalId, so combined with the dead Google fallbacks their events can never be updated or cancelled; video references additionally lose the video credential id, so flows resolving the video credential from the reference (rescheduling Zoom/meet meetings for users with multiple video credentials) can no longer disambiguate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes BookingReference mapping to use `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` (EventManager.ts around the `.map(...)` that builds references). But `CalendarManager.createEvent` only returns `externalId` from its new optional parameter, and in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` the credential-less fan-out path calls `createEvent(c, event)` without supplying that `externalId`, so `result.externalId` will be `undefined` for those created calendar events. Previously the reference used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, so this is a regression that can store null/undefined `externalCalendarId` in references for those flows. Separately, the reference mapping now sets `credentialId` to `undefined` for non-calendar (video) references where it previously used `result.credentialId`, which can break disambiguation for video integrations. These issues are directly implied by the changed signatures/assignments in the diff.
